chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When one is traveling, and the time for prayer enters before he reaches his home, and he continues traveling until he reaches his home, then if he wishes he may shorten (the prayer) and if he wishes he may complete (it), and completing is more beloved to me.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who starts praying while still traveling?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific condition for a traveler's prayer status: if prayer time enters while still on the road, the traveler retains the choice between shortening (qasr) and completing (tamm) the prayer. The Imam’s preference for completion (itmam) highlights the scholarly view that while concession is permitted, full prayer is spiritually superior, a ruling distinct from cases where time enters upon entering the hometown. This establishes the principle that the legal status of 'traveler' persists until the person physically reaches their residential area, regardless of the prayer time's onset.
